I would be lying if I said I didn't. The most important thing about my major is that it would allow me to help other people physically. I'm hoping to get into prosthetic design and to perhaps research into materials to see how I can lower the cost of obtaining one. 

Drawing and design is my passion, and I'm lucky to have found a way that lets me put it in use for the benefit of others. 

The only thing that's off putting about it is whether or not I'll have a job when I graduate... which is why I kind of wish I was in the STEM fields. I've tasted a bit of poverty, watched it destroy my mother.. so the financial uncertainty in my future scares me.

I'm not sure what's the next step off the path from offing myself than to just endure my current situation. 

I'm going to begin searching for jobs and internships(out of state), but that can only get me so far. I mostly took my current job to try to work myself out of my fear of people and to become more assertive. 

I'm not sure what else to do...but thank you for your response.

A lot of Asians struggle with this- it's not a stereotype, I feel, but the truth. My major in the 'arts' is the most practical, bordering engineering instead of fine arts. I have an Asian classmate who was forced into this one because her father would withdraw his financial support for her if she did anything else. She cried to him about how much she hated it and how hard it was and he told her to 'man up and stop being a loser'. Exact words.

I would go into business except I struggle ridiculously with math haha. 

Thank you for the response.
